paper_title: Oral semaglutide 50 mg taken once per day in adults with overweight or obesity (OASIS 1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 to oral semaglutide or placebo through an interactive web-based response system using treatment codes in blocks of four.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated and implemented through a centralized interactive web-response system, masking was maintained with identical products, and baseline characteristics were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to oral semaglutide 50 mg or placebo by trial staff using an interactive web-based response system, which allocated a treatment code to each participant in block sizes of four.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trial staff were masked with visually identical tablets, both groups received the same lifestyle intervention, and efficacy was analyzed by intention to treat regardless of discontinuation or other weight-lowering therapy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy outcomes were assessed in all randomly assigned participants (per the intention-to-treat principle, termed the full-analysis set).

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial retention was high (94%), week-68 bodyweight was observed for 317/334 and 295/333 participants, and prespecified multiple imputation using retrieved-participant data addressed missing values, making material bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Most completed the trial (ie, attended the end-of-trial visit at week 75, regardless of treatment completion; 627 [94%]).

domain_judgments.rationale: Bodyweight is an objective and appropriate outcome measured on the same schedule across groups, and participants, investigators, outcome assessors, and analysts were masked, limiting differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group assignment was masked for participants, investigators, and those assessing outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol and statistical analysis plan were available, coprimary and confirmatory outcomes and estimands were prespecified, and multiplicity was addressed through hierarchical testing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As outlined in the protocol... the coprimary and confirmatory secondary endpoints [were] tested in a prespecified hierarchical order.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low. Centralized randomization, masking, objective outcome measurement, high retention with prespecified handling of missing data, intention-to-treat analysis, and prospective specification and registration support low risk across all RoB 2 domains.

paper_title: Effect of Continued Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Placebo on Weight Loss Maintenance in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: The STEP 4 Randomized Clinical Trial.
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that 803 participants completing the 20-week semaglutide run-in were randomized 2:1 to continued semaglutide or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation is explicit, but the supplied text does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment, and it provides no baseline comparison by randomized group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 803 participants (89.0%) who reached the 2.4-mg/wk semaglutide maintenance dose were randomized (2:1) to 48 weeks of continued subcutaneous semaglutide (n = 535) or switched to placebo (n = 268).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and both groups received lifestyle intervention, with similar adverse-event discontinuation, but differing gastrointestinal effects could reveal assignment and the supplied text does not explicitly establish intention-to-treat analysis or fully describe deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomized, double-blind, 68-week phase 3a withdrawal study... Gastrointestinal events were reported in 49.1% of participants who continued subcutaneous semaglutide vs 26.1% with placebo; similar proportions discontinued treatment because of adverse events with continued semaglutide (2.4%) and placebo (2.2%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was 98.0%, indicating outcome data were available for nearly all randomized participants, although treatment completion was somewhat lower at 92.3%.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 787 participants (98.0%) completed the trial and 741 (92.3%) completed treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, percent change in body weight, is objective and would be measured consistently across randomized groups, making assessor influence unlikely despite potentially revealing adverse effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was percent change in body weight from week 20 to week 68.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and confirmatory secondary outcomes are clearly identified and a trial registration is reported, but the supplied text does not provide a protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan sufficient to exclude selective choice among analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was percent change in body weight from week 20 to week 68; confirmatory secondary end points were changes in waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, and physical functioning.

overall_summary: Overall RoB 2 judgment is some concerns, driven by insufficient detail in the supplied text about sequence generation/allocation concealment, analysis of deviations, and prespecification of analyses. Missing outcome data and objective measurement of body weight present low risk.

paper_title: Effect of Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Placebo as an Adjunct to Intensive Behavioral Therapy on Body Weight in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: The STEP 3 Randomized Clinical Trial.
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group design and states that 611 participants were randomized 2:1 to semaglutide or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is explicit and the large groups appear broadly plausible, but the provided text does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized (2:1) to semaglutide, 2.4 mg (n = 407) or placebo (n = 204).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and both groups received the same behavioral and dietary co-interventions, but treatment discontinuation was differential and the provided text does not clearly establish an intention-to-treat analysis robust to such deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment was discontinued owing to these events in 3.4% of semaglutide participants vs 0% of placebo participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was high, but only 82.7% remained on treatment at trial end and the excerpt does not provide enough information about outcome availability by group or demonstrate that estimates were insensitive to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 611 randomized participants...567 (92.8%) completed the trial, and 505 (82.7%) were receiving treatment at trial end.

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight is an objective and appropriate outcome, appears to have been assessed identically across randomized groups, and double-blinding limits influence from knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, 68-week, phase 3a study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and prespecified co-primary and confirmatory secondary end points are clearly identified, with the reported results corresponding to those end points; no evidence of selective reporting is apparent in the supplied text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The co–primary end points were percentage change in body weight and the loss of 5% or more of baseline weight by week 68. Confirmatory secondary end points included losses of at least 10% or 15% of baseline weight.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by insufficient reporting of sequence generation/allocation concealment and uncertainty about analysis and missing outcome data in the presence of treatment discontinuation. Objective outcome measurement, double-blinding, and prespecified registered outcomes reduce concern in the remaining domains.

paper_title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
design_rationale: The supplied report explicitly describes 1:1 random allocation to semaglutide or placebo using a pseudo-random number generator and an interactive voice response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and implemented through an interactive response system, with balanced baseline characteristics and no important evidence of randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization list was created by a pseudo-random number generator. All personnel and participants were blinded to the treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were blinded with matched devices, premature medication discontinuation was rare and balanced, and the efficacy analysis included all randomized participants using an appropriate mixed model.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All personnel and participants were blinded to the treatment allocation. To ensure masking for all investigators and participants, semaglutide and placebo were administered with the same devices.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome data were available for 98 of 101 randomized participants at week 24, with nearly identical availability and study discontinuation across groups, making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four (7.8%) participants in the semaglutide group and four (8.0%) participants in the placebo group prematurely discontinued study participation due to an adverse event or withdrawal of consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: UACR was an objective laboratory outcome measured identically across groups using three consecutive first-morning void samples, while participant and investigator blinding further limited differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants collected three consecutive first morning void urine samples for urinary biochemistry assessment at baseline and at weeks 20, 22, and 24.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary outcome and analytic model were clearly specified, and the reporting summary states that the primary and secondary outcomes were defined before study initiation, with no apparent selective reporting among eligible analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome defined before the start of the study was the geometric mean change from baseline at week 24 in urinary albumin:creatinine ratio.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low for the primary UACR outcome. Randomization and masking were robust, outcome ascertainment was objective and consistent, missing data were minimal and balanced, and the prospectively specified analysis was reported.

paper_title: Two-year effects of semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity: the STEP 5 trial
design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial using a centrally generated allocation schedule through an interactive web-based response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was centrally generated and implemented through an IWRS, treatment concealment was maintained with visually identical products, and baseline characteristics showed no marked imbalances.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization (1:1) to semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo was done centrally by the clinical research organization (Parexel) in a double-blind manner using an interactive web-based response system (IWRS) with a fixed-size blocking schema, without stratification.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and site staff were masked with visually identical products, both groups received the same behavioral intervention, and the primary treatment-policy analysis included all randomized participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The active product and corresponding placebo product were visually identical to maintain masking of participants and site staff.

domain_judgments.rationale: Week-104 body weight was observed for 89.5% overall but was differentially available between groups (144/152 semaglutide versus 128/152 placebo), and although prespecified multiple imputation was used, missing outcomes could still depend on unobserved weight after discontinuation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, of 304 participants, 282 (92.8%) completed the trial (attended the end-of-trial safety visit), 272 (89.5%) had a body weight assessment at the end-of-treatment visit at week 104.

domain_judgments.rationale: The co-primary outcomes were objective body-weight measurements obtained on the same schedule in both groups, and participants, site staff, and data analysts were masked to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Body weight, waist circumference and vital signs...were measured at baseline; these measurements were repeated every 4 weeks until week 20, and every 8 weeks thereafter, until week 100 and week 104.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the co-primary outcomes and estimands were prespecified, and confirmatory outcomes were analyzed in a predefined multiplicity-controlled hierarchy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The treatment policy estimand quantified the treatment effect among all randomly assigned participants, regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue intervention...and was used to assess the superiority of semaglutide versus placebo for the co-primary and confirmatory secondary endpoints in a predefined hierarchical order.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by approximately 10.5% missing week-104 weight measurements and differential availability between randomized groups despite a prespecified multiple-imputation analysis. Randomization, masking, objective outcome measurement, intention-to-treat analysis, prospective registration, and prespecified hierarchical reporting otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 2·4 mg versus placebo in people with obesity and prediabetes (STEP 10): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre phase 3 trial.
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to semaglutide or placebo through an interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a centralized interactive web-response system, remained concealed and masked until after database lock, and reported baseline characteristics were generally balanced without important differences suggesting randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) to receive semaglutide 2·4 mg or placebo using an interactive webresponse system. ... Treatment allocation remained masked to participants, investigators, and the trial sponsor during the entire trial until after database lock.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked; both groups received the same lifestyle counselling schedule; and efficacy was analyzed by intention to treat regardless of treatment discontinuation, dose reduction, or initiation of other therapies.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment allocation remained masked to participants, investigators, and the trial sponsor during the entire trial until after database lock. ... Efficacy endpoints were analysed using the full analysis set (all randomly assigned participants by intention to treat).

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was high and balanced between groups, missing primary-outcome data were addressed with prespecified multiple-imputation analyses, and sensitivity analyses using different missing-data assumptions were reported to support robustness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 192 (93%) participants completed the trial (128 [93%] in the semaglutide 2·4 mg group and 64 [93%] in the placebo group). ... Several prespecified sensitivity analyses ... using different imputation methods were performed for the co-primary endpoints to assess the effect of missing data.

domain_judgments.rationale: The co-primary outcomes were objective bodyweight and laboratory glycaemic measures, were clearly defined, and were measured in the same way across masked treatment groups, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoints were percentage change in bodyweight from baseline to week 52 and the proportion of participants who reverted to normoglycaemia (HbA <6·0% [<42 mmol/mol] and FPG <5·5 mmol/L) at week 52 with semaglutide 2·4 mg versus placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the protocol and statistical analysis plan were prepared in advance, co-primary outcomes and estimands were prespecified, and the report describes prespecified sensitivity analyses, providing little indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05040971, and is complete. ... Novo Nordisk was responsible for the trial design, preparing the trial protocol and statistical analysis plan, and performing the statistical analyses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low: centralized concealed randomization, double masking, balanced retention, intention-to-treat analyses with sensitivity analyses for missing data, objective outcomes, and prospective registration/prespecification support low risk across all five RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 using a sequence generated by online randomization software, with allocation handled by the secured investigational pharmacy.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated, allocation was restricted to the investigational pharmacy until assignment, and baseline differences were generally small and compatible with chance despite a sex imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study statistician (AS) provided randomisation allocation sequences generated from an online software program (sealedenvelope.com) with a 1:1 ratio and block size of 6 without stratifying factors directly to the investigational pharmacy that was maintained in a locked, secured location.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were masked with identical-appearing injections and standardized procedures, adherence was supported by staff-administered weekly dosing, and analyses followed randomized assignment using intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Key personnel, study staff, participants, and participants’ medical providers were masked to treatment assignment... Analyses were performed using intention-to-treat principles based on randomised treatment assignment including all available data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sixteen participants (14.8%), equally distributed between groups, withdrew before the primary endpoint; the analysis used available data without imputation and asserted missingness was random without presenting supporting sensitivity analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eight participants in each group prematurely withdrew from the study prior to the 32-week primary endpoint... Missing data were random; thus, no adjustments were made for missingness in analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary adiposity outcomes were measured objectively using standardized DXA and CT protocols applied identically across groups, with the radiologist masked to treatment and clinical information.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Measurements were read by a single radiologist (KAG) masked to treatment assignment and clinical information. DXA was performed with a standardized protocol... using the same scanner.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial and protocol were prospectively registered and outcomes were described as predetermined, but seven co-primary outcomes and numerous analyses and transformations create some multiplicity and analytic flexibility, and the supplied report does not establish a fully prespecified analysis plan for every reported estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes were changes in AT quantity by body compartment: 1) total body fat (TBF), 2) limb fat, 3) trunk fat, 4) abdominal TAT, 5) abdominal SAT, 6) abdominal VAT, and 7) pericardial fat... The study was registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04019197).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by 14.8% missing primary-endpoint data analyzed without imputation or reported sensitivity analysis and some potential for selective reporting across multiple co-primary outcomes and flexible analyses. Randomization, masking, adherence procedures, and objective blinded outcome measurement were otherwise strong.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 random assignment to semaglutide or placebo using an interactive Web-based response system, stratified by baseline BMI.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated and implemented centrally through an interactive Web-based system with BMI-stratified 1:1 randomization, and reported baseline characteristics were balanced, supporting an adequate randomization process and concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio with the use of an interactive Web-based response system... Randomization was stratified according to baseline BMI (<35 vs. ≥35).

domain_judgments.rationale: The double-blind placebo-controlled design limited awareness-related deviations, discontinuation rates were nearly identical, participants remained under follow-up after stopping treatment, and efficacy analyses used the full randomized population under an intention-to-treat treatment-policy estimand.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy end points were analyzed in the full analysis population (all participants who underwent randomization, included in the analysis according to the intention-to-treat principle).

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was very high and balanced (97.3% versus 95.5%), few participants withdrew or were lost, and prespecified imputation addressed remaining missing endpoint data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 256 participants (97.3%) in the semaglutide group and 254 (95.5%) in the placebo group completed the trial... The number of participants who withdrew consent or were lost to follow-up was 4 in the semaglutide group and 8 in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured consistently with validated instruments, central laboratory assays, and blinded event adjudication, but major outcomes such as body weight and participant-reported KCCQ-CSS could reveal assignment because semaglutide causes conspicuous weight loss and gastrointestinal effects, potentially influencing subjective symptom reporting despite nominal blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The KCCQ is a standardized, 23-item, participant-administered instrument... [and] an independent external committee, the members of which were unaware of the trial-group assignments, adjudicated hospitalizations for heart failure, urgent visits... and all deaths.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the protocol and statistical analysis plan were available, with prespecified dual primary and hierarchical confirmatory outcomes, multiplicity control, and sponsor-independent validation of the principal results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Details of the statistical methods are provided in the statistical analysis plan (available with the protocol at NEJM.org)... Strong control for type I error was used in analyses of the dual primary and confirmatory secondary end points.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by possible functional unblinding from marked weight loss and recognizable gastrointestinal effects that could influence the participant-reported KCCQ-CSS. Randomization, intention-to-treat analysis, outcome completeness, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 random assignment of 616 participants to semaglutide or placebo in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment and BMI-stratified allocation were reported and baseline differences were broadly compatible with chance, but the provided report does not describe the sequence-generation method or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide at a dose of 2.4 mg or placebo for 52 weeks... Randomization was stratified according to BMI (<35 vs. ≥35).

domain_judgments.rationale: The placebo-controlled trial was double-blind, treatment discontinuation was similar between groups, and efficacy was analyzed in the full analysis population using the treatment-policy estimand according to intention to treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy end points were analyzed in the full analysis population according to the intentionto-treat principle... All analyses in the statistical testing hierarchy were based on the treatment policy estimand.

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was high and balanced (94.2% versus 95.1%), with prespecified single and multiple imputation used for missing outcome values, making material bias from missing data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 292 participants (94.2%) in the semaglutide group and 291 (95.1%) in the placebo group completed the trial... Single and multiple imputation were used to account for missing data.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome measures were appropriate and applied identically across groups, but KCCQ-CSS is participant-reported and treatment-related weight loss or adverse effects could reveal assignment and influence symptom reporting despite nominal double blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The KCCQ is a 23-item, participantadministered instrument that quantifies heart failure–related symptoms, physical function, quality of life, and social function.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered, its protocol and statistical analysis plan were available, outcomes and estimands were prespecified, and hierarchical testing controlled type I error, reducing concern about selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Details of the statistical methods... are provided in the statistical analysis plan (available with the protocol at NEJM.org)... Strong control for the type I error was used for analyses of the dual primary and confirmatory secondary end points.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by absent details on random-sequence generation/allocation concealment and possible functional unblinding affecting the participant-reported KCCQ-CSS. Intention-to-treat analysis, high and balanced follow-up, prespecified imputation, registration, and hierarchical testing otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Efficacy and safety of semaglutide compared with liraglutide and placebo for weight loss in patients with obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo and active controlled, dose-ranging, phase 2 trial

domain_judgments.rationale: A centrally implemented web-response allocation process with blocked, sex-stratified randomization provided adequate sequence generation and concealment, and reported baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomly assigned participants (6:1) ... using an interactive web response system and on-demand allocation with a block size of 56. We stratified the randomisation by sex.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were masked to active versus placebo and the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat, but target dose and escalation schedule were unmasked and recognizable dose-related gastrointestinal effects could have influenced adherence or co-interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to the assigned study treatment, with respect to active versus placebo treatment, but were not masked towards the target dose of drug or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Week-52 bodyweight was available for 93% of randomized participants, with only 7% imputed using a conservative prespecified jump-to-reference method, and observed results were similar to estimated results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 891 (93%) of 957 participants had data available for bodyweight at week 52, and 66 (7%) were imputed in the primary analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively measured bodyweight, assessed repeatedly according to the same visit schedule across groups, making influence from assessor knowledge unlikely despite incomplete masking to target dose.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Bodyweight, vital signs, and adverse events were monitored at every visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the protocol was available, and the primary endpoint and primary intention-to-treat ANCOVA with jump-to-reference imputation were explicitly prespecified, while post-hoc categorical analyses were clearly labeled.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the relative percentage change in bodyweight from baseline to week 52.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by incomplete masking to target dose and escalation schedule and the possibility that recognizable adverse effects affected adherence or behavior. Randomization, objective outcome measurement, outcome completeness, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment allocation remained masked to participants, investigators, and the trial sponsor during the entire treatment and follow-up period and until after database lock.

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial retention was high and week-44 bodyweight outcomes were available for most participants, while prespecified multiple imputation and sensitivity analyses yielded similar findings, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 365 (97%) of 375 participants completed the trial, 244 (98%) of 249 participants in the semaglutide 2·4 mg group and 121 (96%) of 126 participants in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Bodyweight is an objective outcome assessed consistently at prespecified timepoints, and identical-appearing placebo plus masking of participants and investigators reduced the likelihood that measurement differed by allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Semaglutide and placebo solutions for injection were identical in appearance. Treatment allocation remained masked to participants, investigators, and the trial sponsor during the entire treatment and follow-up period and until after database lock.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, primary endpoints and estimands were prespecified, and confirmatory outcomes were analysed through a predefined multiplicity-controlled hierarchy; the added ≥20% weight-loss endpoint was transparently identified as supportive and added before unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary and confirmatory secondary endpoints were tested using a fixed-sequence statistical strategy using a predefined hierarchical order.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low. Randomisation and masking were robust, retention was high with appropriate intention-to-treat and missing-data analyses, bodyweight was objectively measured, and prespecified registered outcomes and multiplicity-controlled analyses limit selective reporting concerns.

paper_title: Semaglutide 2·4 mg once a week in adults with overweight or obesity, and type 2 diabetes (STEP 2): a randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: A double-blind, double-dummy design with visually identical products masked patients and site staff, participants were retained after treatment discontinuation, and the primary treatment-policy analysis followed intention-to-treat principles and accounted for intercurrent events.

paper_title: Semaglutide once a week in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes in an east Asian population (STEP 6): a randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 3a trial

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eficacy outcomes were assessed in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants according to the intention-to-treat principle.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary and confirmatory secondary outcomes were tested according to a predefined statistical testing hierarchy, first for semaglutide 2·4 mg versus placebo followed by semaglutide 1·7 mg versus placebo.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low: randomization and masking were robust, retention and outcome availability were very high, analyses followed intention-to-treat with prespecified missing-data methods, and the prospectively registered outcomes were reported under a predefined hierarchy.

paper_title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Persons with Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis.
design_rationale: The trial explicitly states that 407 participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio using block randomization implemented through an interactive Web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence used block randomization and was implemented through a centralized interactive Web-response system, with reported baseline characteristics generally balanced and no clear evidence of a randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio, with the use of an interactive Web-response system... Block randomization was used (with a block size of six), with no stratification factors.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants received visually identical placebo under double blinding, both groups received the same lifestyle counseling, and the primary treatment-policy analysis included all randomized participants regardless of adherence or additional interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The treatment policy estimand was used to assess efficacy in the full analysis population regardless of adherence to the assigned regimen, use of other interventions, or adherence to pain-medication washout and was used for statistical inference, including confirmatory testing.

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was high and similar between groups, but treatment completion was lower in the placebo group and week-68 missing outcomes were handled by multiple imputation without enough information in the article to establish that missingness could not bias the estimated effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Most of the participants completed the treatment period (86.7% in the semaglutide group and 77.9% in the placebo group) and the trial (90.8% and 89.7%, respectively)... Multiple imputation was performed to account for missing data at week 68.

domain_judgments.rationale: The WOMAC pain instrument was appropriate and applied identically, but the principal pain outcome was participant-reported and substantial, recognizable semaglutide effects could have revealed assignment; perceived assignment was not assessed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Perceived trial-group assignment and the effect of such perception were not assessed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, had a protocol and statistical analysis plan, prespecified primary outcomes and estimands, and used multiplicity control and a hierarchical testing procedure for confirmatory outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The two primary end points were tested at a significance level of 5%, with the alpha split between the two end points... the confirmatory secondary end points could be tested at a 5% significance level in a prespecified hierarchical manner.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by incomplete week-68 outcome data requiring multiple imputation and the possibility that participant-reported pain was influenced by functional unblinding from recognizable semaglutide effects. Randomization, intended-intervention analysis, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

paper_title: Effect of Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Daily Liraglutide on Body Weight in Adults With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes: The STEP 8 Randomized Clinical Trial
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized in a 3:1:3:1 ratio using a blocked allocation schema implemented through an interactive web response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence used blocked randomization through a centralized interactive web response system, which supports random sequence generation and concealment, and the active groups had similar baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized (3:1:3:1) using a blocking schema (block size of 8) via an interactive web response system

domain_judgments.rationale: The active comparison was open-label and treatment discontinuation differed substantially between groups, although both groups received the same lifestyle counseling and the primary treatment-policy analysis included all randomized participants regardless of adherence or rescue intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to semaglutide or liraglutide was not masked (due to dosing differences)

domain_judgments.rationale: Week-68 weight was available for 92.3% of participants with similarly low missingness across active groups, and multiple imputation plus sensitivity analyses indicated that the primary result was robust to missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 92.3% of participants (n = 312) had a week 68 body weight assessment; data were missing for 9 participants in the semaglutide group, 10 in the liraglutide group, and 7 in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight is an objective outcome, and there is no indication that it was measured differently across randomized groups, making bias from the open-label active comparison unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 68.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and had an available protocol and statistical analysis plan, with prespecified primary and hierarchically tested confirmatory outcomes and clearly identified post hoc analyses, leaving little evidence of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: See Supplement 1 and Supplement 2 for the trial protocol and statistical analysis plan, respectively.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by the open-label semaglutide-versus-liraglutide comparison and unequal treatment discontinuation, which could permit deviations related to knowledge of assignment. Randomization, objective outcome measurement, limited and robustly handled missing data, and prespecified reporting otherwise support low risk.
